newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Short stg vol has further to fall-traders.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Short stg vol has further to fall-traders.

text.p: Implied volatility of short sterling options is set to fall further, despite a brief blip up on Thursday and speculation another British rate increase may be on the way, traders said.
"Short sterling vol is going only one way and that is down," said an options broker on the LIFFE floor.
Brokers quoted mid-market implied volatility levels on short sterling options at around 8.60 percent for September, 10.30 percent for December and 12.35 percent for March.
These compared with LIFFE closing levels of 8.19 , 9.84 and 12.00 percent on Wednesday.

Volatility on June options was quoted at 6.40 percent middle, versus 6.16 percent at Wednesday's close but brokers said this was almost irrelevant now as the June futures contract and options expire on June 18.
"Vol has come off so much it is a question of how far can you sell it really," said a trader at a British brokerage.
He said vol could come off a bit further but there was some concern in the market about a possible rate hike, maybe as early as next month.
But brokers said the likelihood was that the Bank of England would hold off.

"The clever money is selling vol at the moment and probably looking for another quarter to a half point base rate hike by the December expiration and a slow rally into the September and December futures," the LIFFE floor broker said.
Brokers said there had been buying of the December 93.50 calls and the 93.25, 93.75 call spread.
LIFFE data showed around 3,000 lots each of the 93.25 and 93.75 December call strikes and around 2,000 lots at the 93.50 December call strike had been traded by 1309 GMT.
The underlying September short sterling future was at 93.24, down one basis point on the day. December futures were at 93.07, also 0.01 lower.
At the long end of the market, brokers said implied volatility on gilt options had come off a touch during healthy activity.
In particular, brokers noted paper sellers of the September 114-00 puts.
